- If sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.8) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to match sentiment momentum.  
- If sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.3) in recent days, model tends to overreact — reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price spikes — especially after sentiment turns positive — apply a 5–10% upward bias to forecast for 3–5 days post-spike.  
- Model overestimates early in the 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive — adjust downward by 2–5% for first 5–7 days.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., sharp drop after peak), model often fails to correct — add a 3–5 day lagged mean-reversion buffer in forecast.  
- When sentiment history shows repeated high positive values, model tends to overfit recent trend — apply smoothing or reduce slope of forecast for next 7 days.
